method: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass. Reopened the adopted International Sociology table and choice/admission footnotes, Culture major entries, placement and Culture thesis before comparing the source-led reconstruction with the exact finished selections, contributions, alignments and audience contract. Reconsidered the strongest positive and negative evidence rather than only replaying validators. This is analytical separation by the same AI, not an independent person or live rendering.
findings: The current programme and adopted I-42–I-44 International Sociology table confirm the English track and 60+60+60 EC. Culture in Comparative Perspective is first-listed and continues the target’s comparative cultural identity. All four major courses and the Culture-specific twelve-credit project and thesis variants agree. No Dutch Urban Issues component or second major is added.

The 42-credit non-exchange mobility window consists of twelve-credit placement, eighteen genuinely open credits and twelve restricted credits. The I-43 footnote permits two courses from the non-selected major; Globalization and Social Risks and Global Migration are the first two in the public Social Risks menu and both are six-credit permitted subjects. No minor is invented. The two Autumn electives with the flexible placement and six open EC, followed by Spring thesis, Social Philosophy and twelve open EC, provide a coherent ordinary arrangement.

Placement requires at least 336 hours, approved plan and signed contract before starting, relevant organisational work, supervision and a reflective pass/fail report. The Culture thesis is individually empirical, written in English, usually using suitable secondary data within available supervisory expertise, with proposal, peer feedback, article-style report and symposium. The adopted rule is the completed propaedeutic phase PLUS sixty postpropaedeutic credits; completing the first two years meets it. The ordinary Spring path is used, not exceptional Autumn entry. Skills and methods progression is preserved without inventing prerequisites that contradict the concurrent questionnaire/project semester.

The actual major is cultural sociology of reproduction, individualisation and secularisation; constructed identities and power; climate narratives and meaning; and European families in macro-level social change. The closest UCR composition materially responds through sociology, social psychology, gendered/racial/Indigenous histories, documentary inquiry, international institutions and rights, with qualitative, statistical and survey research. It supplies meaningful comparative-cultural inquiry despite the explicit gaps in dedicated family sociology, migration, projects and disciplinary thesis. Related historical and legal study is a specified complementary contribution, not a claim of equivalent regional or disciplinary scope.

The two additional options respond to four eligible interests each: social risk uses climate science, governance, welfare, health, policy and causal inquiry; inequality/policy uses political institutions, economic mechanisms, data/econometrics, health and public communication. The closest owns the other nine eligible interests. All 47 rows were reconciled and example/outcome references removed from construction basis. Substantive priorities change actual courses; each pair exceeds four courses/thirty credits each way. The maximum-three stopping decision remains justified.

Six substitutions strengthen the existing concepts and repair four original offering conflicts. Current descriptive evidence for American Century research and Renaissance art was fully considered without assuming missing enrichment makes them unavailable. Documentary, psychology, statistics, ethics, policy and econometrics offer stronger specific contributions here. All 36 selected course identities and contributions, actual offerings and prerequisites, 24 unique courses per option, four per term, first-year PPD and six advanced courses pass. The survey contribution uses the actual Psychology of Leading Under Pressure course rather than a stale diversity-management name.

Fifteen partial alignments now follow actual course content. Behavioural modelling fits causal methods, data workflows fit Skills 3, academic writing fits Skills 2 and a designed psychological survey gives a bounded relationship to psychometric questionnaire methods. Culture/race, constructed identity and climate-narrative relationships distinguish their scope. Twelve explicit gaps retain family sociology, separate projects and epistemology, placement, open and restricted study and individual thesis. Optional research is outside the scheduled credits. No forced one-to-one coverage or generic project-to-thesis equivalence remains.

Read the clean International Sociology title, 27 component labels, seven selected notes, three labels/concepts, fifteen partial relationships, twelve gaps, all audience references and all 36 selected descriptions against the existing renderer mapping and actual bytes. Exact unchanged shared description reviews are reused; case-specific roles are newly assessed. The source button and additional current official sources support the selected pathway. No app/renderer, workbook or enrichment changes and no local Shiny/browser activity, screenshots, modals or release approval are claimed.
